solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Mindful of concussion? Not entirely bothered

indicators.note: bothered, in the sense of stirred up or flustered, signals that the remaining letters are jumbled
not entirely says the word concussion loses its final letter

explanation.surface: Someone checks whether a blow to the head has left them shaken, deciding it is not too bad.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Not entirely' trims CONCUSSION to CONCUSSIO, and 'bothered' rearranges those nine letters.
explanation.definitionFit: Being aware of something is the same as being mindful of it; the adjective takes 'of' in both cases.

clue.text: Animal bed without a hint of insulation

indicators.note: without in its old sense of outside: the bed goes around the letter a

parts.note: a cot is a small bed

indicators.note: hint of means just the first letter of insulation is taken

explanation.surface: An animal's bed lacks any trace of insulation, so it sleeps cold.
explanation.walkthrough: 'without' looks like 'lacking' but means 'outside', putting COT round A to make COAT, then I is added.
explanation.definitionFit: The coati is a long-snouted raccoon relative from the Americas.

clue.text: Plant providing food served up around island close to South America

indicators.note: close to puts the next pieces right beside the first group
around has the reversed food wrapped round the island letter
in a down clue, served up has the word read from bottom to top

parts.note: scran is British slang for food

explanation.surface: A plant supplying meals sits near an island off South America.
explanation.walkthrough: 'served up' reverses the food word and 'around' wraps it round I. Scran is British slang for grub; 'close to' is read as 'next to', setting the last letters beside the rest.
explanation.definitionFit: Narcissus is the botanical genus of daffodils and jonquils, a flowering bulb.

clue.text: Examinees worried by last of questions on unfinished novel

indicators.note: on, in an down clue, places the following pieces after the novel
unfinished means the novel's title loses its final letter

parts.note: Candide is Voltaire's satirical novel
ate, as in 'what's eating you?', means worried

indicators.note: last of takes only the final letter of questions

explanation.surface: Students sitting a test fret over the final question about a half-read book.
explanation.walkthrough: The novel is Voltaire's Candide, cut short by 'unfinished'. 'Worried' as ate comes from 'what's eating you?'.
explanation.definitionFit: Candidates are the people sitting an examination, so examinees is a plain synonym.

clue.text: Without thought for sick worker

parts.note: someone off work is ill, so off can mean sick
a hand is a manual worker, as on a farm or ship

explanation.surface: Someone shows no consideration for an employee who is unwell.
explanation.definitionFit: An offhand remark is casual and careless, made without thought.

clue.text: Left over right, together with a couple of supports at the front

indicators.note: at the front puts those two letters before the rest
a couple of takes just the opening two letters of supports

parts.note: plus means together with

explanation.surface: Instructions for leaving something over the right-hand side, with two props placed in front.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Left over' looks like a direction to put L above something, but it is the definition. 'a couple of' takes the first two letters of 'supports' and 'at the front' puts them first.
explanation.definitionFit: A surplus is an amount remaining beyond what is needed, so it is what is left over.

clue.text: Unsuitable for an unmarried woman

parts.note: an is the indefinite article, giving the letter a
Miss is the title of an unmarried woman

explanation.surface: Something is deemed inappropriate for a single woman.
explanation.definitionFit: Amiss means wrong or out of place, as in 'nothing amiss', close to unsuitable.

clue.text: Book's verifiable truths initially ignored

indicators.note: initially ignored drops the first letter of the word for truths

parts.note: facts are verifiable truths

explanation.surface: A book's checkable claims have been overlooked from the outset.
explanation.walkthrough: The 's stands for 'is' joining definition to wordplay.
explanation.definitionFit: The Acts of the Apostles is a book of the New Testament, usually called just Acts.

clue.text: Senseless getting involved with half- hearted girl

parts.note: to be in something is to be involved with it

indicators.note: half-hearted removes half of the double letter at the heart of the name

parts.note: Anne is a girl's name

explanation.surface: Someone foolish is dating a woman whose heart is not in it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'half-hearted' takes one of the two central N's from ANNE.
explanation.definitionFit: Inane means silly or lacking sense, a straightforward synonym of senseless.

clue.text: Begin to suspect deception in small rate changes

indicators.note: changes, read as a verb acting on the preceding words, says those letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Someone grows suspicious of trickery when they notice tiny adjustments to a rate.
explanation.definitionFit: To smell a rat is an idiom for sensing that something is wrong or that someone is cheating.

clue.text: In favour of wearing almost any piece of protective clothing

indicators.note: wearing means the first piece has the second around it like a garment
almost means the word any loses its last letter

parts.note: pro means in favour of

explanation.surface: Someone would support donning whatever protective garment is available.
explanation.walkthrough: 'almost' drops the last letter of 'any'; 'wearing' means the favour word has that pair on round it.
explanation.definitionFit: An apron is worn over clothes to protect them from mess, as in a kitchen.

clue.text: Enthusiasm to embrace street art abroad is excellent

indicators.note: to embrace means the word for enthusiasm wraps around the jumbled letters

parts.note: fire means passion or enthusiasm

indicators.note: abroad, in its sense of all over the place, signals the letters are scattered

parts.note: ST, the abbreviation for street, joined to art gives the letters to shuffle

explanation.surface: Passion for graffiti seen overseas is called outstanding.
explanation.walkthrough: 'abroad' looks like it places the art overseas, but it scrambles the street abbreviation with 'art'; 'to embrace' wraps the enthusiasm word round them, just before its final letter.
explanation.definitionFit: First-rate means of the highest class or quality, a synonym of excellent.

clue.text: Small back on essentially big piece of furniture is unique

indicators.note: on joins the furniture to what comes before it
back means the word for small is reversed

parts.note: mini means small

indicators.note: essentially takes the core, the middle letter, of big

parts.note: a table is a piece of furniture

explanation.surface: A small backrest on a large piece of furniture makes it one of a kind.
explanation.walkthrough: 'back' turns MINI into INIM; 'essentially' gives I, the centre of 'big'.
explanation.definitionFit: Something inimitable cannot be copied, so it is matchless or one of a kind.

clue.text: Soldiers avoiding distressing experience in town

indicators.note: avoiding means the soldiers' letters are left out of the experience

parts.note: an ordeal is a painful or distressing experience
OR, other ranks, means ordinary soldiers

explanation.surface: Troops steering clear of a traumatic episode in some town.
explanation.walkthrough: OR, other ranks, is the usual crossword term for soldiers who are not officers. DEAL is a seaside town in Kent.
explanation.definitionFit: Deal is a coastal town in Kent, in south-east England, so it is an example of a town.

clue.text: Agree to modify drop scone recipe

indicators.note: to modify says these letters are changed into a new order

parts.note: R, for the Latin recipe, is the abbreviation used on prescriptions

explanation.surface: A baker agrees to adjust the instructions for griddle cakes.
explanation.walkthrough: A drop scone is a small pancake. R stands for recipe, the Latin 'take' heading a prescription.
explanation.definitionFit: Things that correspond match or tally, which is one sense of agree.

clue.text: Reject conflict with first of appeals for love

indicators.note: with marks the letter that comes in
for marks the letter it replaces, the one meaning love

parts.note: discord means conflict or strife
love is zero in tennis, the letter O

indicators.note: first of takes the opening letter of appeals

explanation.surface: Someone spurns a fight, along with the lead appeal on behalf of love.
explanation.walkthrough: In DISCORD the O (love, from the tennis score) is swapped for A, the start of 'appeals'.
explanation.definitionFit: To discard something is to throw it away as unwanted, which is to reject it.

clue.text: Prepared to take exercise on the way up and down

indicators.note: to take means the first word takes the reversed letters inside it

parts.note: food that is dressed has been prepared

indicators.note: in a down clue, on the way up means the letters read from bottom to top

parts.note: PE is physical education, exercise at school

explanation.surface: Getting ready to work out climbing and descending.
explanation.walkthrough: 'on the way up' reverses the exercise letters, since this is a down entry, and 'to take' puts them after the first letter of the word for prepared.
explanation.definitionFit: Feeling down means feeling low or sad, a sense shared with this adjective.

clue.text: Salesman taking large amounts in recession as a bung

indicators.note: in recession means going backwards, so the joined words are read in reverse
taking joins the large amounts onto the salesman

parts.note: a rep is a sales representative
pots means large amounts, as in pots of money

explanation.surface: A sales rep makes lots of money in an economic slump through a bribe.
explanation.walkthrough: 'bung' looks like British slang for a bribe, which fits the salesman, but here it is a plug.
explanation.definitionFit: A bung is a plug or cork for closing a hole or bottle, which is what a stopper does.

clue.text: Recommend the use of oddly neglected Greek writer after a bit of persuasion

indicators.note: after places the Greek writer after that letter
a bit of takes only the first letter of persuasion
oddly neglected drops the odd-numbered letters of Greek, keeping the even ones

parts.note: a scribe is a writer or copyist

explanation.surface: Someone advises reading a forgotten Greek author once gently coaxed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'oddly neglected' leaves R and E, the second and fourth letters of 'Greek'.
explanation.definitionFit: A doctor who prescribes a treatment advises or orders its use.

clue.text: Obtain endless drink on ship

indicators.note: on joins the ship after the drink
endless means the drink loses its last letter

parts.note: a posset is a hot drink of milk curdled with ale or wine
SS is the abbreviation for steamship

explanation.surface: Someone gets hold of an unending supply of drink aboard a vessel.
explanation.walkthrough: A posset is an old hot drink of milk curdled with wine or ale; 'endless' cuts it to POSSE.
explanation.definitionFit: To possess something is to have or own it; one sense of obtain is to come to hold.

clue.text: Unnerve Arab leader speaking at university

indicators.note: at joins the university piece after the sound
speaking means the word for the leader is taken as it sounds

parts.note: a sheikh is an Arab chief or leader
up means at university, as in 'up at Oxford'

explanation.surface: An Arab chief giving a speech at a university disturbs people.
explanation.walkthrough: One common pronunciation of SHEIKH rhymes with 'make'. 'Up' is British usage for being at university.
explanation.definitionFit: To shake someone up is to upset or rattle them badly, a phrasal synonym.

clue.text: Up-to-date course

definitions.meaning: ... affairs are those happening now, so ... here is the adjective modern
the course or flow of a river or electricity

explanation.surface: Up-to-date course.
explanation.definitionFit: As an adjective it means present-day; as a noun it is a stream or flow following a course.

clue.text: Control over medical examination

parts.note: to check something is to control or restrain it
up and over both mean finished, as in 'time is up'

explanation.surface: Supervision of a doctor's examination.
explanation.definitionFit: A checkup is a routine examination by a doctor or dentist.

clue.text: Essentially disregarding Patel's first language

indicators.note: disregarding means that letter is left out of the Latin phrase

parts.note: per se is Latin for in itself or essentially

indicators.note: first takes the opening letter of Patel

explanation.surface: At heart, ignoring a politician's mother tongue.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Essentially' looks like an extraction signal for a middle letter but is PER SE; dropping P leaves the Gaelic tongue.
explanation.definitionFit: Erse is an old name for the Gaelic tongue of Scotland or Ireland.

clue.text: Become established as a consequence of joining clique

indicators.note: joining sets the clique alongside the other piece

parts.note: a set is a clique or social circle
in, as in 'in consequence of', can mean as a result of

explanation.surface: Taking root as a result of becoming part of an exclusive group.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in consequence of' is the idiom behind reading the first phrase as 'in'.
explanation.definitionFit: When weather or a condition sets in, it begins and takes hold, so it becomes established.

clue.text: Bags of plunder in Vatican City share- out

indicators.note: in means the plunder sits inside the shuffled letters
out, as in a share-out, means the letters are dealt about and rearranged

parts.note: V is the international vehicle code for Vatican City
to sack a town is to plunder it

explanation.surface: Sacks of loot are divided up in the Vatican.
explanation.walkthrough: 'share-out' splits: 'out' scrambles 'share' with the Vatican City letter, and 'in' sets the plunder inside, before the final letter.
explanation.definitionFit: Haversacks are canvas bags carried on the back or shoulder.

clue.text: Stop harnessing atomic energy

indicators.note: harnessing means the word for stop holds the letter inside it

parts.note: to stem a flow is to stop it

explanation.surface: Halting the use of nuclear power.
explanation.walkthrough: 'harnessing' looks like a power-generation verb but is the containment signal.
explanation.definitionFit: Steam is the vapour that drives engines, so it stands for energy or vigour, as in 'run out of steam'.

clue.text: Make out after international game

indicators.note: after places the spotting word after the abbreviation

parts.note: to spy something is to catch sight of or make it out

explanation.surface: Discern something following an international match.
explanation.definitionFit: This is a children's guessing pastime where players name something seen beginning with a given letter.

clue.text: Against interrupting call for help on top of mountain as it were

indicators.note: on top of joins the mountain right after the distress call
interrupting means the word for against breaks into the distress call

parts.note: SOS is the distress signal
to can mean against, as in 'face to face' or 'put shoulder to the wheel'
a peak is a mountain top

explanation.surface: A distress signal breaks off at a summit, more or less.
explanation.walkthrough: 'interrupting' puts the word for against inside the distress call; 'on top of' sets the mountain after it.
explanation.definitionFit: So to speak is a phrase used to mark words as figurative, meaning in a manner of speaking.

clue.text: Contributing to iconic exhibition being postponed

indicators.note: Contributing to says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: A piece forms part of a landmark exhibition that has been delayed.
explanation.definitionFit: A plan put on ice is shelved or deferred, an idiom for postponement.

clue.text: Fine period of success in North Dakota? Just the opposite

indicators.note: in says one piece goes inside the other
just the opposite reverses the stated containment, so the state goes inside the period

parts.note: a day, as in 'every dog has its day', is a period of success
ND is the abbreviation for the US state of North Dakota

explanation.surface: A good spell in an American state, or rather the reverse.
explanation.walkthrough: Read literally, the period would go inside the state; 'Just the opposite' turns that round so the state goes inside.
explanation.definitionFit: Dandy is informal, chiefly American, for fine or excellent, as in 'everything is just dandy'.

clue.text: Fanciful plan of Dickens' protagonist formed on reflection to capture Fred's heart

parts.note: Pip is the hero of Dickens's Great Expectations

indicators.note: to capture means the reversed word holds the central letters
on reflection means the word for formed is read in a mirror, backwards

parts.note: made means formed

indicators.note: heart takes the central letters of Fred

explanation.surface: A Dickens hero's wild scheme takes shape after he reflects on Fred's feelings.
explanation.walkthrough: 'on reflection' reverses MADE to EDAM, which captures RE, the heart of 'Fred'.
explanation.definitionFit: A pipe dream is an unrealistic hope or fantasy, an idiom from opium smoking.
